 Appearance:
Shri Sameer Verma - Advocate for the appellants.
Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for the respondent.

Order 
This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 29.04.2011 passed in Claim Case No. 78/2009.

The challenge is on two counts, first that the insurance company has wrongly been exonerated from the liability to pay compensation and second that the quantum of compensation has wrongly been assessed by the Claims Tribunal.
2. I.A.No. 12155/2025 is an application for dispensing with service on the owner and driver of the insured vehicle.

3. In view of the fact that despite paying process fees on several occasions, respondents No. 1 and 2 are deliberately avoiding service of notice of this appeal and also it is seen from the record that the appellants have repeatedly sent notices on the address which was recorded in the claim petition before the Tribunal, the service was affected on the same address in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35720 2 MA-1583-2011 the claim petition before the Tribunal and it is the case of the appellants that respondents are still residing on the same address but they are deliberately avoiding the service, the application for dispensing with service on respondents No. 1 and 2 is allowed and the appeal is heard in their absence.
4 . The short facts of the case are that on 21.05.2009 at around 04:30 in the evening, deceased Paru was going in jeep from Rampura to his home Choti Heerapur.

When the jeep reached near Dawar Petrol Pump, the pick up vehicle bearing registration No. MP-45-G-0389, being driven by respondent No.1 in rash and negligent manner ran into the jeep in which deceased Paru was travelling due to which he sustained grievous injuries, he succumbed to those injuries ultimately.

sentences.text: The claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act was filed by the appellants/claimants claiming compensation for the death of Paru before the Claims Tribunal.
It was stated in the claim petition that the deceased, on the date of accident was earning Rs. 150/- per day and additionally an amount of Rs. 25,000/- from agricultural work.

The Tribunal after recording evidence concluded that it was the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the insured vehicle which caused the accident, hence a total compensation of Rs. 1,84,500/- was awarded.
5. The Tribunal while quantifying the amount of compensation has taken the income of the deceased Paru at Rs. 15,000/- per annum on notional basis.
The insurance company was exonerated from liability to pay compensation on the ground that the driver of the insured vehicle was not having a valid licence so also the absence of fitness certificate.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35720 3 MA-1583-2011 Tribunal has wrongly concluded that the vehicle was being plied in breach of terms of the insurance policy.
He points out that it has come on record that the driving licence (Exh. D/7) was available which was a licence for LMV.
The vehicle in question was a pick up having weight less than 7500 kg.

As such in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case o f Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663 as well as M/s Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd.vs. Rambha Devi & Ors.
reported in (2025) 3 SCC 95 , the person holding LMV licence is eligible to drive such vehicle.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: M/s Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd.vs. Rambha Devi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, on this ground exoneration could not have been done.

7. As regards fitness certificate, learned counsel for the appellants submits that valid driving licence was available and even if it is taken to be true that there was absence of a valid fitness certificate, pay and recover should have been directed.
As regards the quantum of compensation, learned counsel submits that the claim before the Tribunal was that the deceased was earning Rs. 150/- per day.

If the Tribunal was of the opinion that there was no sufficient material to prove the same, still the income of the deceased could not have been taken below the minimum wages for an unskilled labour which was Rs. 3,000/- per month at the relevant point of time.
He thus prays for enhancement of compensation not only for loss of dependency but even for other non-pecuniary heads.

8. Learned counsel for the appellants further submits that the Claims Tribunal has incorrectly held that it is a case of composite negligence hence in terms of para 29, the Tribunal directed that the respondent No.1 owner of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35720 4 MA-1583-2011 the vehicle shall pay half of the amount of compensation.
He submits that this was a totally incorrect conclusion of the Claims Tribunal.

He submits that even if it is admitted that it was a case of composite negligence, then also it was a choice of the claimant to implead either both of them or any one of them for claiming compensation.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.2/insurance company submits that present is a case of contributory negligence because the deceased was hanging from the jeep and was not sitting inside the same.

He refers to the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in para 19 and submits that it has clearly been recorded that deceased Paru was hanging outside the jeep as has been stated Smt. Tejlibai And 6 Ors. vs Mukam Singh And Anr. on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48938641/
2 by the eye witness of the accident.

entities.text: Smt. Tejlibai And 6 Ors. vs Mukam Singh And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is thus clear that he was contributing to the accident.

He further submits that the claimants did not lead any evidence to prove the income of the deceased,
hence the Tribunal has taken the income correctly at Rs. 15,000/- per annum.

As regards the liability of the insurance company, he submits that at the relevant time the award was passed, the pronouncement of law by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Mukund Dewangan a n d Rambha Devi (supra)was not there.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan a n d Rambha Devi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, the decision was made by the Tribunal as per the law which was in force function at the relevant time.
Hence, he submits that on this count also no interference is required to be made and the insurance company should not be saddled with the responsibility to pay compensation.
10. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the record.

11. From perusal of the record, it is clear that the respondents NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35720 5 MA-1583-2011 themselves exhibited the driving licence of the driver of the insured vehicle (Exh. D/7) which is for LMV.

In view of the authoritative pronouncement of law by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Mukund Dewangan and Rambha Devi (supra) this issue is no more res integra that a person holding LMV licence can also drive a commercial vehicle having weight less than 7500 kg.
In the present case, the insured vehicle was undisputedly a pick up vehicle having total weight of less than 7500 kg.
As such, it is hereby held that the driver of the vehicle was having a valid licence to drive the insured vehicle.
12. On perusal of the record of the Claims Tribunal it is also clear that there was absence of valid fitness certificate.

However, the issue with respect to liability of the insurance company to pay compensation even if there is absence of valid fitness certificate is no more res integra as this Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Manoj and Ors., 2014 ACJ 2389 in para 9 has held as under :
''9.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Manoj and Ors., 2014 ACJ 2389
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After hearing Mr. Manoj Jain, in the considered opinion of this court, as per the defence taken by the insurance company, the violation of the terms and conditions of the policy has been pleaded due to non-availability of fitness certificate.

As per the company, it is clear that no such condition has been specified in the policy, however,
merely non-production of the fitness certificate would not prevent (sic) the finding recorded by the Tribunal.

In addition to the aforesaid, it may safely be observed that until and unless violation of the conditions stipulated under section 149 has been specified and established before the Tribunal, the finding of joint and several liability so recorded does not suffer from any illegality, warranting interference in this appeal.

In view of the foregoing discussion, in the considered opinion of this court, the appeal filed by the appellate is devoid of any substance, hence dismissed in limine.''
13.

Considering the case of Manoj (supra) , the position of law was reiterated by this Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Sunita Markam & Ors., 2022 ACJ 1799 in para 8 of the judgment which is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35720 6 MA-1583-2011 reproduced below :

sentences.text:
In the present case, admittedly, till the accident took place, permit was not cancelled and even otherwise permit is not mandatory for a fire brigade as is apparent from clause (c) of sub-section (3) of section 66 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 and once it is held that permit is not mandatory, then the issue of fitness, on which permit depends, becomes secondary.
Even there is no condition in the insurance policy laying down that absence of fitness certificate will be a ground to repudiate the policy.

Therefore, when these facts are cumulatively taken into consideration, then appeals are, admittedly, devoid of merit in as much as there is an exception in clause (c) of sub-section (3) of section 66 of Motor Vehicles Act and so also in the light of the judgment of the Indore Bench of this court in the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Manoj (supra).''

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Manoj
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. Although, in the case of Sunita (supra) there were some facts which was distinguishable from the facts of the present case, however, there is a clear fact available on record that in the insurance policy, there was no condition with respect to the fitness certificate.

The Division Bench of High Court of Karnataka while considering this aspect of absence of fitness certificate has considered the provisions of Section 56, 84 and 86 of Act of 1988 and concluded that Section 86(1) of the Act provides that if any condition of permit specified in Section 84 of the Act is breached,
then also the competent authority is required to given an opportunity of hearing to the holder of the permit before cancellation of registration.

entities.text: Division Bench of High Court of Karnataka
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is thus, clear that absence of fitness certificate would not absolve the insurance company from its liability to pay compensation.

15. Although reliance has been placed by the learned counsel for the insurance company on the judgment of jurisdictional High Courts, however in view of the two decisions as aforementioned passed by the Coordinate Benches of this Court, it is hereby held that the insurance company is liable to pay compensation.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35720 7 MA-1583-2011 16.

As regards the quantum of compensation, it is seen from the evidence that the Tribunal has assessed the income on notional basis at the rate of Rs. 15,000/- per annum which in the considered view of this Court is not correct.

Though, it is correct that there was no evidence to establish that the deceased was earning Rs. 150/- per day, however if there was absence of any material to prove his income then in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Hans Raj Vs.
Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., passed in SLP (C) No.3511 of 2020 the support of the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority can be taken which provides that at the relevant time minimum wages for unskilled labour were Rs. 3,000/- per month.

entities.text:

Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, the income of the deceased is taken at Rs. 3,000/- per month.

Considering the age of deceased as 26 years on the date of accident, 40% increase is made in his income under the head of future prospect in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

As there are seven number of dependents, as such deduction is modified for personal expenses to 1/5th and as per his age and law laid down in the case of Sarla Smt. Tejlibai And 6 Ors. vs Mukam Singh And Anr. on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48938641/
4 Verma (Smt.) and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier of 17 is applied.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, the total compensation for loss of dependency would now come to Rs. 6,85,440/-.
17.
The claimants are widow, four children and mother & father of the deceased.
As such all of them are entitled for compensation for loss of spousal, parental and filial consortium.
As such all seven of them are hereby awarded Rs. 40,000/- each which totals to Rs. 2,80,000/-.

Apart from this,
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35720 8 MA-1583-2011 Rs. 15,000/- each is awarded for funeral expenses and loss of estate.

Thus, the total compensation would now come to Rs.9,95,440/-.
18.
However, considering the fact that the deceased Paru was hanging outside the vehicle at the time of accident, he is held to be contributing to the extent of 25% in the accident.
As such, for contributory negligence, deduction of 25% is made from the aforesaid total amount of compensation.
Now the payable amount of compensation comes to Rs. 7,46,580/-.
19. The learned insurance company has informed that an amount of Rs. 50,000/- has been paid under No Fault Liability.
Thus, after deducting the said amount, the appellants be paid an amount of Rs. 6,96,580/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
If any amount has already been paid, then the same be adjusted accordingly.
20. As this Court has held hereinabove that the insurance company is liable to pay compensation thus it shall pay the amount of compensation as quantified hereinabove, however.
With the aforesaid, appeal stands allowed to the extent indicated hereinabove and disposed of.
(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE vidya Smt. Tejlibai And 6 Ors. vs Mukam Singh And Anr.
